summary: Today’s pulse tracks Israel strikes south Lebanon after two soldiers killed by explosion, US Senate committee votes to hold Fauci in contempt over Covid hearing, and EasyJet agrees to £5.7bn takeover by US firm. Across BBC and Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are killed, dyson, and south. In the background, Israel charges West Bank settler over death of renowned Palestinian activist and South Yorkshire man who killed lodger and hid body in concrete gets 35-year sentence keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Israel strikes south Lebanon after two soldiers killed by explosion
headlines.description: Lebanese authorities says one person was killed in the strikes, which came after the first Israeli military fatalities in Lebanon in more than a month.

headlines.title: US Senate committee votes to hold Fauci in contempt over Covid hearing
headlines.description: The committee will now refer him for possible prosecution for refusing to answer questions about his handling of the Covid-19 pandemic.

headlines.title: EasyJet agrees to £5.7bn takeover by US firm
headlines.description: The no-frills carrier agrees to be bought by US firm Apollo after a rival suitor drops out.

headlines.title: Israel charges West Bank settler over death of renowned Palestinian activist
headlines.description: Yinon Levi faces trial for reckless manslaughter related to the 2025 killing of Awdah Hathaleen Israeli prosecutors have charged a Jewish settler over the killing of a Palestinian community leader in the occupied West Bank last year- the ⁠first such indictment in nearly three years. In papers filed by the state attorney’s office, Yinon Levi is charged with reckless manslaughter in the death of Awdah Hathaleen, a prominent ⁠activist who was involved in the 2025 Oscar-winning documentary No Other Land.

headlines.title: South Yorkshire man who killed lodger and hid body in concrete gets 35-year sentence
headlines.description: Christopher Wright, 73, shot Richard Dyson in November 2019 and then dismembered his remains A man who killed his lodger and concealed his dismembered body in a barrel filled with concrete for more than five years has been jailed for a minimum of 35 years. Christopher Wright, a 73-year-old farmer from South Yorkshire, was convicted in July in Sheffield crown court of murdering Richard Dyson, 55, in 2019. Dyson had been living in his car on Wright’s farm in Hoyland and had been doing jobs for the then 67-year-old when the pair had a falling out.

headlines.title: Trump denies US weapons shortage and says information 'leakers' being 'hunted down'
headlines.description: While precise data is classified, publicly available information suggests the US has used up many difficult-to-manufacture weapons.

headlinePool.title: India-Bangladesh relations hit new low over exiled PM’s speech to press in Delhi
headlinePool.description: Dhaka accuses India of giving platform to a ‘convicted genocider’ by allowing Sheikh Hasina to address journalists Bangladesh has lashed out at India for allowing the ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina to address journalists in New Delhi, plunging already strained bilateral relations to a fresh low. Dhaka accused India of giving a platform to a fugitive it labelled a “convicted genocider” and of undermining efforts to repair ties, after Hasina vowed to return to Bangladesh in December despite facing a death sentence on charges of “crimes against humanity”.

headlinePool.title: Top Ugandan footballer killed by robbers armed with paving stones
headlinePool.description: David Owori, who played for the national team, died in hospital after he tried to stop robbers taking his phone The Ugandan football community is in mourning after the death of a player who was fatally injured during a robbery in the capital, Kampala, on Tuesday night. David Owori, who captained Sports Club Villa, a Uganda Premier League club, and represented the national team, was attacked after resisting an attempt to steal his mobile phone and other belongings.

headlinePool.title: Senate committee holds Anthony Fauci in contempt of Congress – live
headlinePool.description: Republican majority voted to hold the retired health official in contempt after hearing where he repeatedly invoked the fifth amendment Republicans hold just 53 seats, making it almost certain to fall short of that threshold. The Senate homeland security and governmental affairs committee voted to hold Anthony Fauci in contempt of Congress after a bitter hearing last week, where the retired public health official invoked the fifth amendment for fear of self-incrimination and possible prosecution by Republican lawmakers, who have routinely vilified him for his handling of the Covid-19 response.

headlinePool.title: Reform will jail directors of companies employing illegal workers for up to five years, says Yusuf – UK politics live
headlinePool.description: Party says employers would be held responsible even if they were unaware of the worker’s immigration status A Reform government will introduce national licensing for vape shops, which Zia Yusuf says will see a decrease of 70% in the businesses on British high streets. “We will also end financial disincentive,” he says. Reform will establish a central prosecution fund for local authorities to pursue businesses employing illegal workers. Corporate CEOs have been making a fortune by hiring illegal workers and undermining British youngsters. Reform will jail them and stop illegal working for good - we will stand up for British workers.

headlinePool.title: Iran says a deal with Oman to reopen the strait of Hormuz is close to being finalised – Middle East crisis live
headlinePool.description: Under the proposed agreement Tehran would control inbound traffic according to reports Understanding reached on coordinates for shipping route through Hormuz, Iran says Donald Trump’s Board of Peace, which was set up in January to oversee the reconstruction of Gaza , has finally issued its first construction contract in the devastated territory: a project to build a rudimentary 150-person military outpost to house Moroccan troops, a source familiar with the matter told the Guardian. The contract, which has not yet been finalised, was awarded to Arkel International, a Louisiana-based firm that has previously carried out work with the US government in countries such as Iraq.

headlinePool.title: Greetings from a wildlife park in central Sri Lanka that's a haven for elephants
headlinePool.description: At a time of increased conflict between elephants and humans, as elephant habitats are converted to intensive agriculture, the Hurulu Eco Park is a place where the animals can graze unimpeded.

headlinePool.title: Ceuta residents ‘sad, helpless, anxious’ as up to 5,000 migrants remain in the city, president says – Europe live
headlinePool.description: Juan Jesús Vivas has been briefing EU lawmakers on the ‘humanitarian emergency’ and says updated death toll now lies at least 100 people The commission also got repeatedly asked about last week’s events in Ceuta and media reports that social media accounts seen calls for another attempt to overwhelm the border on 15 August. A spokesperson said the commission was aware of various threats to the EU’s external border, and “that’s why we need to step up our work.” “I can point you to the solar eclipse next week on the 12th, which will have an impact on energy production. We have established a operational group that is dedicated to the preparation of this and … my understanding is that they have a meeting tomorrow, Friday, where they are preparing for possible impacts.

headlinePool.title: Foster + Partners cleared over man’s death when window fell from London penthouse
headlinePool.description: Crown court rules architecture firm not responsible for fatal incident but project managers and engineers found guilty of safety breaches The architecture firm founded by Norman Foster has been cleared over the death of a man killed by a window that fell 90 metres from a newly constructed London penthouse. Foster + Partners, the practice behind some of the world’s most recognisable buildings such as the Gherkin and revamps of the British Museum and Germany’s Reichstag, were not held to be responsible for the death of Mick Ferris , a 53-year-old coach driver, in 2018.

headlinePool.title: DR Congo river boat under quarantine for Ebola after five deaths
headlinePool.description: The health minister says all the passengers are being screened as a precautionary measure.
